what_its_for: Rifampin is an antibiotic used to treat or prevent tuberculosis (TB). It is also used along with other medicines to treat certain other serious bacterial infections, such as those caused by Staphylococcus (staph). It works by stopping the growth of bacteria in your body.
how_to_take: Take rifampin by mouth, usually once a day on an empty stomach — either 1 hour before a meal or 2 hours after a meal. This helps your body absorb the medicine better. Swallow the capsule whole with a full glass of water. If you have trouble swallowing capsules, you can open the capsule and mix the contents with applesauce or jelly. Always take it at the same time every day to keep a steady level of medicine in your body. Do NOT skip doses, even if you feel better, because not finishing your full course of treatment can allow bacteria to grow back and become harder to treat.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your weight, age, and the condition being treated. A common adult dose for TB is 600 mg once a day. For children, the dose is based on body weight. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions and never change your dose without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store rifampin capsules at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C and 25°C). Keep the bottle tightly closed and away from light, heat, and moisture. Do not store in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of the reach of children and pets. Dispose of any expired or unused medicine safely — ask your pharmacist about drug take-back programs in your area.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking rifampin, as it can increase the risk of liver damage. This medicine can make your birth control pills less effective — use a backup method of contraception such as condoms while taking this medicine. Rifampin can turn your urine, sweat, tears, and saliva an orange-red color — this is harmless but can permanently stain contact lenses, so avoid wearing them while on this medicine. Avoid taking antacids within 1 hour of taking rifampin. Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before starting any new medicines, including vitamins and herbal supplements, because rifampin can interact with many other drugs.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency help if you experience: yellowing of your skin or eyes (signs of liver problems), dark urine or unusual tiredness, severe stomach pain or vomiting, skin rash, itching, or hives, unusual bruising or bleeding, fever or chills that are new or get worse, vision changes, or signs of a severe allergic reaction such as swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat, or difficulty breathing. Also tell your doctor if you notice flu-like symptoms such as muscle aches, chills, or headache, especially if you are taking this medicine less than daily.
when_it_works: It may take several weeks before you start feeling significantly better, especially if you are being treated for TB. It is very important that you keep taking this medicine for the full length of time prescribed by your doctor — treatment for TB can last 6 months or longer. Do not stop taking it just because you feel better. Stopping too soon may allow the infection to come back and be much harder to treat.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Talk to your doctor before taking rifampin if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. It is generally used during pregnancy only if clearly needed, as it may affect the baby. Breastfeeding: Rifampin can pass into breast milk. Talk to your doctor about the risks and benefits. Liver disease: Tell your doctor if you have liver disease or a history of liver problems, as rifampin can affect the liver. Regular liver function blood tests may be needed. Elderly patients: Older adults may be more sensitive to side effects, especially liver problems. Children: Rifampin can be used in children, but the dose is carefully adjusted based on weight.
